I'd like to thank you for the opportunity to introduce the 2024 Civic Services Survey results. As a bit of background administration has conducted surveys for many years.

In 2018, we moved to two surveys rather than one to better manage the survey length. These surveys include the Civic satisfaction and performance survey and the performance priorities and preferences survey.
In 2014, the surveys were conducted by foreign research in May and June and both included 800 online panel responses.
For each online survey, respondents were selected at random from a professional panel. Given the random sampling efforts, the data is considered reliable.
Further, the data is also representative of Saskatoon's population based on two demographic factors, those being age and gender.
The online methodology and consistency for most survey questions allow for trend in comparison analysis relative to previous years.
The surveys reflect our collective efforts to understand residents' perception of how they feel about their city and how we are serving the community.
These findings are used to inform decisions related to strategic priorities, budgeting and service delivery, as well as highlighting opportunities for continuous improvement.
I'm pleased to share some encouraging insights from the Civic satisfaction and performance survey. First, a strong majority of residents, 84% expressed satisfaction with living in Saskatoon.
This truly stands out and shows the overwhelming sense of pride and overwhelming sense of pride in our community.

The measurement to quality in life encompasses several aspects of well-being. Some of these factors include physical health, wealth, employment, education, recreation, leisure time, social belonging, safety and more.
In 2024, a majority of residents, 72% indicate the quality of life in Saskatoon is good or very good.
Although Saskatoon did experience a slight decline in this area from previous years, it appears to be reflective of trends in Canada.

For example, a 2024 city of Calgary, municipal benchmarking study showed that the municipal norm of cities for quality of life ratings, being 63%, this doesn't seem to be unique to Saskatoon, but we still have a solid foundation to build upon.
A majority of 75% are also satisfied or very satisfied with the quality of services that are provided by the city.
Further, 78% rate the value of services they receive from the city as good or very good.
The survey also helps to identify opportunities to improve by understanding the most important issues respondents fill are facing our city.
In 2024, the most significant mentions included homelessness by 23% of respondents, crime, public safety and policing by 21% of respondents.
The topic of homelessness is also not unique to Saskatoon.
Upon a review of several different municipal civic services surveys for 2024, it showed that homelessness was frequently excited as an important issue by other cities.
For example, in Calgary, this was cited by 17% of respondents, London, Ontario 54%, Cologne of 41%, Vancouver 23%, any health effects 21%.
In the second survey, a satisfaction with 31 different city services was measured on a scale of 1 to 10.
Overall satisfaction remains high. However, we saw particularly high scores in the areas of reliability of electrical services, quality of drinking water and fire protection.
These same services were also identified as a city's key strengths along with speed of water main break repairs and garbage collection.
In planning for the future, the areas where respondents would like to see the city provide more service, included affordable housing, road maintenance, stone ice management and policing.

The majority of respondents would also like to see us maintain the same level of service for fire services, garbage collection and waste reduction, park maintenance and recreation and cultural programs.

So these are just a few of the highlights. In summary, while there's room for continuous improvement and planning opportunities, the 2024 survey results do again reflect that solid foundation for our future.
The two appendices included in the report provide a summary of each of the survey results for 2024.
The detailed research reports that were completed by forum research are available on Saskatoon's website at Saskatoon.ca.
The next surveys are planned to start again this year in May and June.
